archetype.name: Rebuilding (outshot and outfinished)
archetype.definition: A young Chicago group that is losing the puck battle at 5-on-5 and getting below-average goaltending, with too little scoring talent in the lineup to cover either.

report.headline: The league's worst team on merit, with the bounces making it look even worse
report.take:
Chicago is 4-13-1 and last in the league in Goal Diff / GP at -2.06. That last place is not a fluke. The Blackhawks rank 32nd in goals a game and 31st in goals allowed. They hold 40% of the expected goals at 5-on-5 (31st) and 44% of the shot attempts (30th). They take 22.9 shots a game against a league average of 27.4 and give up 30.3. All three roster groups grade F, F and D-. The site's 31st-of-32 rank is a fair read.

The season is getting worse, not stabilising. The last 10 games went 1-8-1, the last five 0-4-1, and November is 0-4 with 5.75 goals allowed a game, capped by a 2-9 loss in Carolina. Some of that slide tracks who has been available. Connor Bedard, the best player on the roster by Game Score (11.3) and points (14), has played only 12 of the 18 games. Bowen Byram has played six, though at 24.7 minutes a night when he does. Without Bedard there is little offense: Patrick Kane has one goal on 25 shots, and the forward group's listed players have 30 goals combined.

The numbers do hide something, and it is regression upside, not a better team. All-situations PDO is 96.6, dead last, against a league norm of 100.6. Skaters are shooting 9.4% against a league 11.6%, and the goalies are stopping 87.2% against 89.1%. Last year's team had a 5-on-5 PDO of 99.6 and Goalies GSAx of +7.5. This year's GSAx is -10.2, and most of that damage comes from Arvid Soderblom's four starts (-6.1, .842). Spencer Knight at .881 is below average but not a disaster. Some of the goals-against bleeding should ease.

The process, though, is worse than the last two years. xGF % was .431 in 2024-25 and .424 in 2025-26. It is .40 now. Those teams finished with 61 and 72 points. This one is on pace for 41. Better luck lifts that, but the underlying share of play says this is a bottom-two team that has to wait out the rebuild. It is not a sleeper.

strengths.title: Penalty kill holds its ground
strengths.body: At 78.6% the PK ranks 11th, above the league's 77% average. It is the one unit not getting overwhelmed. It also has a track record: .793 two seasons ago and .836 last year. That makes it the most repeatable thing on this team, even with poor goaltending behind it.

strengths.title: Bedard and Kantserov carry the offense
strengths.body: Bedard's Game Score of 11.3 in 12 games is easily the team's best, and he ranks 95th on the centers tab. Roman Kantserov leads the team with 9 goals on 31 shots while logging 18.46 minutes. Bedard's production should hold. Kantserov's finishing rate is likely to cool, given his 37.1% xGF share.

concerns.title: Badly outplayed at 5-on-5
concerns.body: A 40% xGF and 44% CF mean Chicago spends most of its even-strength time defending. The shot counts confirm it: 22.9 for, 30.3 against. The opposition is cashing in from everywhere. Chicago ranks 31st in points allowed to wingers, to defensemen and to forwards overall relative to those players' norms. This is a talent and structure problem, and it is worse than last season's .424.

concerns.title: Goaltending swung from asset to liability
concerns.body: Goalies GSAx went from +7.5 last season to -10.2, 30th in the league. Soderblom's -6.1 in four starts is the sharpest hole, and Knight's .881 and -2.1 are below par as well. A .872 combined save % behind a team allowing this many shots is a brutal mix. Knight should drift closer to average, but this group grades D- for a reason.

concerns.title: Power play is producing nothing
concerns.body: At 9.8% the power play is last in the league, well under the 22.5% average. It has fallen from .249 two years ago and .169 last season. The listed defensemen have 2 PP points combined, so there is no point shot to speak of. Bedard's return helps, but the decline predates this year.

trend.note: A competitive-ish October (4-9) gave way to an 0-4 November. The last five games went 0-4-1 with 5.6 goals allowed a game, worse than the season rate by 1.38.

weekAhead.headline: Two home games against leaky goaltending and soft penalty kills
weekAhead.body:
This is as soft a stretch as the schedule offers, both games at home. Buffalo is 8-6-3 but sits 19th on the site with a -0.41 goal differential a game. Its record is propped up by close-game luck: Pts vs Goal Diff of 2.3 ranks 3rd. Buffalo also controls play (6th in CF % at 53%) behind an A- blueline, which is a bad matchup for a team that cannot hold the puck. Winnipeg, 27th on the site, is the better chance for a win. The Jets allow a league-worst 33.2 shots a game and carry D+ goaltending at .881.

Both opponents' penalty kills rank 25th or worse, so if Chicago's last-place power play is ever going to wake up, it is this week. The realistic bar is one win and keeping the goals against below the recent spiral. A split would count as progress.

keyMatchups.title: Chicago PP vs weak kills
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo kills 71.2% (26th) and Winnipeg 71.7% (25th). Chicago's 9.8% power play has nowhere easier to find goals. Even a couple of conversions would swing these games.

keyMatchups.title: Possession gap against Buffalo
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo's 53% CF share ranks 6th, and Chicago's 44% ranks 30th. Expect the Blackhawks to be pinned in their own zone again. Buffalo's .880 save % (27th) is the equaliser if Chicago gets its few looks on target.

keyMatchups.title: Winnipeg gives up volume
keyMatchups.body: The Jets allow 33.2 shots a game, last in the league, and points to defensemen at a 27th-ranked rate. This is the night Chicago's low shot totals could actually rise and its blueline could chip in.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Bedard is in the lineup and the power play finally converts against two bottom-eight penalty kills.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect modest improvement on the current pace, not a turnaround. A 96.6 all-situations PDO sits far below the league's 100.6, and shooting and save percentages that depressed tend to climb. A full season of Bedard, who has missed a third of the games, also raises the floor. That should pull the final total above the 41-point pace. But a .40 xGF share is worse than the two seasons that produced 61 and 72 points, so the ceiling is roughly where those teams finished, and probably below.

The penalty kill is the sustainable piece. The 5-on-5 deficit and the thin forward depth are not going away without roster changes the sheet gives no hint of. Chicago looks set to finish at or near the bottom of the Central and the league.
swingFactors: Power play recovering from last place

confidence.note: Only 18 games, but possession, shots, goaltending and results all point the same way.
